messages:
incidents-bot: PAGER: oncall-auth alerted — Ember (VPC private) report: spike of 502s from tenant bridge, token introspection failing against customer identity proxy. Auto-severity: high. Please ack and triage. :rotating_light:

samira (oncall-auth): acked. I'm pulling logs and traces now. Are we seeing introspect 401s or TLS handshakes?

diego (infra): seeing TLS handshake errors from our side to Ember's identity proxy: 'tlsv1 alert unknown ca' and some 'certificate verify failed' lines. Could be client cert expired or chain changed.

nate (customer-ops): Ember liaison reports they rotated their upstream CA last night and applied a new leaf cert. They thought we were using JWKS for OIDC only, but there's an mTLS client cert used for the tenant bridge.

samira (oncall-auth): ok that matches. Our bridge to Ember uses mutual TLS for the tenant identity proxy. If their server replaced CA and didn't include intermediates we might reject. Can someone fetch the cert chain with openssl to validate?

diego (infra): running quick check: ```openssl s_client -connect identity.ember.internal:443 -showcerts -CApath /etc/ssl/certs``` getting cert chain, looks like they served only leaf. No intermediate CA. Also the subjectAltName includes the expected host.

victor-sre: Ember's cert chain missing intermediate -> our mTLS verification library fails when validating chain against our system CAs. Short-term mitigation: allow bridge to fall back to JWKS-only validation for this tenant while Ember fixes chain. That requires a config change on the tenant-routing proxy — I can push a targeted override. Impact: tokens validated via introspect/JWKS rather than mutual TLS assertion; still requires token validity checks.

samira (oncall-auth): what's the customer impact window? Are customers blocked for all traffic or only some flows?

augie-support: Ember reported elevated errors for all auth-requiring API calls for ~12 minutes, many customers retried and some timed out. No data plane compromise reported.

nate (customer-ops): Ember requests we do not rotate their consumer cert or do any churn on our side. They will push correct full chain within next 20 minutes.

samira (oncall-auth): plan: 1) apply temporary tenant override to relax mTLS chain enforcement (failover to JWKS introspect) for Ember; 2) coordinate with Ember to push correct chain; 3) monitor errors and revert override when chain is corrected; 4) create follow-up: ensure we warn customers about missing intermediates in onboarding. I will own the temporary override.

victor-sre: noted. I'll prepare the canary config payload and list of instances to update. Need approval to touch tenant-route config.

samira (oncall-auth): approved. Keep it narrow to tenant ID ember-542. No global changes.

diego (infra): pushing the override to the proxy canaries now, limiting to 2 pods in us-east-1. Command: ```robinctl deploy --env prod --proxy tenant-route --selector tenant=ember-542 --patch '{"auth":{"mtls":{"allow_incomplete_chain":true}}}'```

incidents-bot: deploy job started by diego (infra). Job id: dpl-9932.

victor-sre: can we add a short lived feature-flag so revert is easy? Put TTL 30m on this override.

samira (oncall-auth): yes add ttl. diego add ttl=30m. Confirm when live.

diego (infra): patch applied to 2 canaries, verifying. Logs show successful JWKS-based introspect calls now. Error rate on ember tenant down to baseline within ~90s on those canaries.

augie-support: Ember confirms partial traffic recovered. Monitoring observing 95% reduction in 502s for ember-542 sessions hitting patched pods.

nate (customer-ops): Ember will roll their full chain in ~12 minutes and report back. They asked for a short post-incident note about rotating CAs without intermediates.

samira (oncall-auth): monitoring: observed a few token mismatch retries — we should watch for replay/failing sessions but so far no auth bypass. Notify security if anything suspicious.

victor-sre: I'll open a short-lived alert to catch abnormal token issuance patterns for ember-542. Adding a pulse chart to the incident dashboard.

incidents-bot: alert created: ember-542-token-anomaly.

ember-customer-liaison: Ember confirms they've uploaded the proper intermediate cert to their edge and restarted identity proxy 2 minutes ago. "We've corrected the chain and validated with curl."

samira (oncall-auth): diego, run a health check across all proxy pods and if their backends now present full chain, revert the override early.

diego (infra): running scripted checks: ```for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l tenant=ember-542 -o name); do kubectl exec $pod -- openssl s_client -connect identity.ember.internal:443 -showcerts | sed -n '1,20p'; done``` Results: full chain now present from all 6 pods.

victor-sre: confirming metrics — success after full rollout. No further 502 spikes in the last 6m.

samira (oncall-auth): good. Reverting override now. diego, remove TTL override and roll the config back to strict chain validation.

diego (infra): rollback command applied, canaries then full rollout. incidents-bot: deploy job started by diego (infra). Job id: dpl-9933.

incidents-bot: deploy job dpl-9933 succeeded.

augie-support: Ember confirms traffic looks normal from their side. Customer impact window: ~12 minutes with partial outages during rotation.

nate (customer-ops): I'm preparing the customer-facing summary and suggested remediation steps for Ember to avoid recurrence (include cert chain validation in their CI).

samira (oncall-auth): assigning sev: high -> downgraded to sev: mitigated. Logging postmortem task: include action items: 1) add tenant onboarding checklist to detect mTLS chain completeness; 2) build automatic intermediate fetch/validation step in our tenant bridge; 3) doc for customers about timely intermediate certs; 4) review our fallback policy for JWKS vs mTLS and document risk tradeoffs. I'll own the post-incident.

victor-sre: also add a small enhancement: when we detect 'unknown ca' error, surface a targeted runbook link in the incident message with the exact openssl command and mitigations.

ember-customer-liaison: thanks everyone for the quick help. We'll add cert chain validation to our deploy pipeline and notify the infra team when we rotate next time.

samira (oncall-auth): handing off to next oncall for post-incident follow-up: victor-sre, you're on for the next 4 hours to monitor ember-542 dashboards and start postmortem doc.

victor-sre: taking handoff. Will kick off the postmortem doc and tag relevant teams.

incidents-bot: handover logged. Next oncall: victor-sre.

samira (oncall-auth): closing pager. If anything reappears ping the incident channel or re-open pager. :white_check_mark:
